questions.q: Explain the factors that control the climate of India.
answer: Several factors together shape India's tropical monsoon climate.

answer.text: The Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle of India, making the south tropical and the north subtropical. The high Himalayas shield the country by blocking cold winds from Central Asia, keeping it warmer than places at similar latitudes.
The seasonal reversal of winds, or monsoon, along with the shifting pressure belts and jet streams, governs the rainfall.

Areas near the sea have a moderate, maritime climate, while the interior has an extreme, continental one. Mountains like the Western Ghats force moist winds to rise, giving heavy rain on the windward side and a dry rain shadow on the leeward side.

questions.q: Describe the four seasons of India's climate.

answer.text: From December to February, skies are clear and cool north-east winds blow; the north-west gets some rain from western disturbances and the south-east from the retreating monsoon.
From March to May, temperatures rise and local storms occur — the hot loo in the north, the Kaal Baisakhi in Bengal, and pre-monsoon mango showers in Kerala and Karnataka.
From June to September, the south-west monsoon, arriving with a sudden burst, brings most of India's rainfall through its Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal branches.
In October and November the monsoon withdraws, giving rain to the Tamil Nadu coast, and cyclones may strike the Bay of Bengal coast.

questions.q: How does the monsoon work, and why is it called a unifying bond for India?

answer.text: is the seasonal reversal of winds that brings India most of its rain, driven by the differential heating of land and sea.

list: In summer the land heats up, creating low pressure that draws moist winds from the sea — the southwest monsoon brings rain from June to September
In winter the winds reverse and blow from land to sea — the northeast monsoon
The arrival ('burst') and retreat of the monsoon set the rhythm of the year

answer.text: because the whole country waits for and depends on it.

list: Farming, festivals and water supply across India revolve around the monsoon
Its rhythm ties the varied regions of India into a single seasonal cycle

questions.q: Why is rainfall in India so unevenly distributed, and how does this affect people's lives?

answer.text: varies greatly from place to place because of relief, distance from the sea and the path of the monsoon winds.

list: The windward Western Ghats and the northeast (Mawsynram, Cherrapunji) receive very heavy rain
Areas in the rain shadow, like western Rajasthan and the interior Deccan, get very little
Rainfall also varies from year to year
Regions of low or uncertain rain face drought and crop failure
Areas of heavy rain may face floods, so water management is vital across India
